lede: A fortnight ago Robert D'Arcy was a rank, a burial and a rumour of Yorkshire, and his family was a list of names on a tree. He now has a marriage, a career in five gazetted steps, a funeral reported in seventeen newspapers — and a household. This page assembles it.
parents: First commissioned 17 January 1776 as Practitioner Engineer and Second Lieutenant, Corps of Engineers · Major 1802 · Lieutenant-Colonel 1 March 1805 · Colonel 1813 · Major-General by 1827 · died Chatham 13 May 1827, buried there with military honours on the 19th, aged 76
Baptised SOUTH LEITH, Midlothian, 19 July 1754, daughter of JOSEPH WARD and MARTHA GAIRDEN · buried Chatham 1823, aged 66

children.b: born 14 March 1780 · baptised Portsea St Mary, 19 March 1780
children.note: Royal Artillery from about 1795. St Domingo 1793, Sicily, Walcheren, and five years in Persia in the service of Prince Abbas Mirza. Lieutenant-Colonel, K.L.S. Died at Home Mead, Lymington, 7 February 1848, leaving his property to his wife Catherine and five children.

Married JOHN MADDOCK JONES of Pen-y-bryn, Ruabon, Major of the Royal Denbigh Militia, at Chatham in 1806, her brother JOSEPH signing as witness. She died at Le Havre in February 1843 and he at Ingouville near Havre the following month. Her death notice calls her “daughter of the late MAJOR-GENERAL D'ARCY, R.E.” — the only record anywhere that gives Robert a corps as well as a rank.

children.b: born 18 February 1783 — the tree says “Portsmouth, Hampshire, England OR WEST INDIES”, and hedges for a reason
children.note: 39th Foot. Married MISS LUDLAM OF GUERNSEY, announced September 1805 in a notice calling him “son of Lieut. Colonel D'Arcy”. Peninsular War 1808. In Ireland with the regiment 1820 and 1822. Married secondly Maria, and sailed for New South Wales on the convict ship England in April 1826. THE LINE THIS ARCHIVE DESCENDS FROM.

Aged 57 and living in Joseph's house at Priestlands in 1841. Of exactly the right generation, in exactly the right household — and no other record of him has been found anywhere in Hampshire. Portsea's transcript stops in 1782, so a baptism of 1784 could never have been found in it.

children.b: born February 1786 · christened ST MICHAEL, BARBADOS, 18 February 1786
children.note: Son of Robert and Jane, christened in Barbados while his father served there. Gentleman Cadet to Second Lieutenant, Corps of Royal Engineers, 1 February 1804; First Lieutenant 1 March 1805, in the same Ordnance Office announcement that made his father a Lieutenant-Colonel. Buried Chatham St Mary, 9 May 1805, aged nineteen. The Kentish Gazette of 14 May calls him “the son of Col. D'Arcy, chief engineer of Chatham lines” and says he was interred with military honours — the same words used of his father twenty-two years later.

children.b: born 15 December 1787, BARBADOS · christened St Michael, 17 March 1788
children.note: Christened in the same Barbados parish as Constantine, to the same parents. DOCUMENTED 14 September 2026: died in the BRIGHTON registration district in the first quarter of 1875, AGED 87 — which matches her recorded birth of 15 December 1787 exactly. In 1841 she was keeping house in Brighton with her two sisters.

The third of the Barbados children. DOCUMENTED 14 September 2026: “On the 23rd ult., at BEDFORD SQUARE, BRIGHTON, MISS CATHARINE D'ARCY, aged 86” — Horsham, Petworth, Midhurst and Steyning Express, 8 February 1876. Her death is registered at Brighton in the first quarter of 1876 and she left an estate: Death Duty Register, TNA IR 27/396.
Died 24 October 1791, aged five months. The first Anna Maria.

Named for the sister who had died the previous autumn, and dead herself in 1800 aged seven. Her birthplace matters beyond her short life: by October 1792 the family is back in Portsmouth, which brackets the West Indies posting at the far end.

The youngest, and the only one born in the West Country. DOCUMENTED 14 September 2026: died in the BRIGHTON district in the second quarter of 1869, aged 73. NOT to be confused with the CHARLOTTE D'ARCY christened at Chatham in 1826 — that one is her niece, George Pitt's daughter, who sailed for New South Wales eight days later.

portsea: Only one of them was baptised at Portsea, and this archive spent months reading that as meaningful. It is not: FindMyPast's Hampshire collection covers Portsea St Mary continuously from 1770 to 1792 and returns Joseph and nobody else — so the others were christened wherever the Corps had posted him. A regiment moves; a parish register does not follow it. AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY FOUND WHERE TWO OF THEM WERE, AND HAD NOT PUT IT HERE. Constantine was christened at St Michael, Barbados in 1786 and Jane in the same parish in 1788 — inside the twenty-four-year gap between Robert's first commission and his next gazetted promotion. That has been on the Hornby page since the summer while this page called Constantine unplaced.
shape: Ten children in fourteen years, born in three places on two sides of the Atlantic: four at Portsmouth, three in Barbados, one at Lyme Regis. Two died small and were both called Anna Maria. Two sons went into the artillery and the infantry and a third into his father's Corps of Engineers, where he died at nineteen. Three daughters ended their lives in and around Brighton, one of them at eighty-eight. It is the ordinary shape of a service family, scattered by the postings that made it.
open: Robert's own parentage — and whether the CONSTANTINE D'ARCY of 1759–1778, whom the tree makes his brother by the same two parents, is a real sibling or this family's own Constantine duplicated and back-dated.
Whether Richard was his son, which needs a baptism from a parish this archive has not yet identified.

What became of the two ANNA MARIAS beyond the tree's dates — both died as children. Their three surviving sisters are now documented: JANE, CATHERINE and CHARLOTTE lived together in Brighton and died there between 1869 and 1876.
When exactly Robert went to Barbados. His children's birthplaces put him there by 1786 and home by 1792; the Board of Ordnance papers would say.

And who ELIZABETH PITT was — living in Joseph's house in 1841, dying at Lymington in 1851, and sharing a surname that ran through four generations of this family. This is the one question the archive's own material could not help with.
Where Jane, Catherine and Charlotte were in 1851, 1861 and 1871 — they are in the Brighton census in 1841 and in none of the three that follow, under any spelling.
crossread: Five of these children were added on 14 September 2026, not from any new record but from this archive's own family tree — read, for the first time, against this archive's own open questions.

portraits.lab: Berta Ruck, Ancestral Voices (London, Hutchinson, 1972) — list of illustrations, plates between pp.128–129
portraits.head: Their photographs were printed in 1972, by a descendant, and nobody here had looked for her
portraits.body: The GEDCOM notes this archive inherited quote «by Berta Ruck» in two places and nobody had asked who she was. She was the novelist Berta Ruck (1878–1978), and she was descended from this family: FreeBMD gives «RUCK, Arthur Ashley» and «D'ARCY, Elizabeth Eleanor» at the same volume and page — Penzance, September quarter 1877, GRO 5c 381 — and Berta was born the following year. In 1972 she published a family memoir, and its list of plates is a roll-call of this page.
plates: The Three Aunts D'Arcy — Jane, Kate and Charlotte
One of the Three Aunts in Persian dress, brought home by her brother Joseph
Amy Darwin, née Ruck, and Charles Darwin
portraits.gives: It settles a name the tree could not. The GEDCOM hedged «Anne Heevish or Hewish Adams» for the woman Robert West married at Bombay in 1846. Three records that did not copy each other now agree: the India Office ecclesiastical return indexes her ANNE H ADAMS, the Gentleman's Magazine announcement calls her ANNIE ADAMS, and her great-niece's plate list names her ANNIE HEWISH D'ARCY, NÉE ADAMS. An initial in a government index, a forename in a magazine and a caption under a photograph, and between them a woman has her whole name back.
portraits.careful: What is NOT established. That Berta Ruck is the daughter of that 1877 marriage is an inference from a date and a father's name, not a record, and whose daughter Elizabeth Eleanor was is not established at all. The «C.B.» after Robert D'Arcy's name is a caption written by a descendant in 1972 and not an official list — a first pass over the Gazette for 1814–1830 did not find it, though that OCR mangles this surname badly. And the book's text is in copyright and lending-restricted: only the plate list was read. Borrowing needs an account and none was made.
portraits.hidden: It has been invisible for fifty years because the Internet Archive catalogues it under the subject «Dorsey family», a mangling of D'Arcy. No search for the surname will ever surface it.
